source_text_analysis.description: Torah LM2 #121 is a very brief oral teaching (5 lines) transmitted by Reb Nosson. Its argument is entirely practical advice about prayer: (1) the Rebbe encouraged followers who found prayer very difficult; (2) he pointed to the example of a convert, who considers it a great merit to merely recite the words of prayer up to 'Baruch She'amar'; (3) he advised a simple person to think of himself as needing to rectify only one small section of prayer at a time, section by section, based on the idea of gilgulim (reincarnations) — perhaps he already completed the other sections in a previous life; (4) the general rule is to pray a little at a time with kavana rather than trying to hold all of the prayer in mind at once; (5) it has already been explained elsewhere that each person prays a section of prayer 'according to their bechina' — for there are 'masters of hands' and 'masters of feet,' etc.
source_text_analysis.bechina_language_check: The text uses the word 'בְּחִינָתוֹ' once, in line 5: 'כָּל אֶחָד מִתְפַּלֵּל אֵיזֶה חֵלֶק מֵהַתְּפִלָּה לְפִי בְּחִינָתוֹ'. This is the grammatical/possessive form — 'according to his bechina [level or aspect]' — not the structural equation form 'X הוא בחינת Y'. It asserts that individuals differ in spiritual level, not that two named concepts are parallel expressions of the same underlying reality. This phrasing does not generate a bechina edge.
